name: Slack
summary: Easy to start: turn on public distribution and any workspace can install. The catch for agents: unlisted apps get 1 request per minute on message history unless listed in the Slack Marketplace, which needs 10+ active workspaces and a review of up to 10 weeks.
scenario: An agent that reads channel history and posts messages in customers' Slack workspaces.

composio.note: Check the Composio managed OAuth directory. Composio suggests your own app for Slack when users should see your name on the consent screen.

portal.accountNeeded: A Slack account in a development workspace you can install apps into.

policyAndDomain.detail: Not needed for unlisted distribution beyond HTTPS redirect URLs; Marketplace listing needs listing materials.

userCapBeforeApproval.detail: No install cap for unlisted apps, but strict rate limits on history methods (see nuances).

adminApproval.detail: Some workspaces require admin approval for installs or allow only Marketplace apps.

appReview.detail: For this scenario (reading history in customer workspaces), Marketplace listing is effectively required: unlisted apps get 1 request/min and 15 messages per call on history methods. Posting-only agents can skip review.

securityAssessment.detail: No third-party assessment; Marketplace review includes Slack's own checks.

time.note: The wait applies only if you list in the Marketplace: up to 10 business days for preliminary review, then up to 10 weeks for functional review of a new app. Unlisted distribution has no wait.

nextStep: Create the app at api.slack.com/apps, add bot scopes and your HTTPS redirect URL, install it in your own workspace, then activate public distribution.

prerequisites.text: HTTPS for redirect, events and interactivity URLs before enabling distribution.
For Marketplace: installed on 10+ workspaces active in the last 28 days, plus support readiness.

steps.title: Create the Slack app
steps.detail: At api.slack.com/apps create an app from scratch or from a manifest and pick a development workspace. An agent can write the app manifest for you.

steps.title: Add scopes and redirect URL
steps.detail: Under OAuth & Permissions add bot or user token scopes and your HTTPS redirect URL (e.g. Composio's). Request only what you use; admins weigh scopes when approving.

steps.title: Install in your workspace
steps.detail: Install to the development workspace and test reading and posting.

steps.title: Activate public distribution
steps.detail: Manage Distribution → complete the checklist → Activate Public Distribution. You get an Add to Slack button and shareable install URL.

steps.title: Decide on Marketplace listing
steps.detail: If your agent reads message history at scale, plan for Marketplace listing: reach 10 active workspaces, then submit for preliminary and functional review.

review.summary: Optional Marketplace review. Unlisted apps install without review but face reduced limits and some admins only allow Marketplace apps.
reviewersCheck: App works fully and is publicly available
Scopes match real features; broad scopes like search:read or admin.* get pushback
review.meanwhile: Distribute unlisted to pilot customers; internal apps keep normal limits.

blockers.issue: Agent can only fetch 15 messages per minute from history.
blockers.fix: Since May 29, 2025 new unlisted commercial apps get 1 request/min and 15 objects per call on conversations.history and conversations.replies. List in the Marketplace, or build as an internal app for a single customer.
Some admins allow only Marketplace apps or require approval; ask the admin to approve or pursue listing.
Remove scopes for unbuilt features, fix bugs, and provide reviewer install access rather than your own credentials.

nuances.text: Turning off public distribution uninstalls the app from every workspace except your own.
Existing installations of older unlisted apps keep their previous rate limits; new installs get the new ones.

uncertainties: Marketplace review times vary with volume; Slack shows an estimate on the submission page.

sources.title: Slack changelog: Rate limit changes for non-Marketplace apps (May 2025)

corrections: Original assumption was 'easy, optional review'. The May 2025 rate limits make Marketplace listing close to required for history-reading agents, so the score now ranges Easy to Medium.
